title: Introduce timebound RBAC approval flow, KMS geofence prover, and audit-hash signer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Customers operating across regulated jurisdictions asked for a mechanism to require operator approvals that are both timebound and auditable, plus stronger proof that KMS requests originated from a pinned geofence. This PR implements three coordinated features: 1) a timebound RBAC approval queue (RBAC v2 extension) that allows policy authors to declare ephemeral grants with explicit TTLs and approval steps; 2) a KMS geofence prover that validates location assertions from edge gateways and attaches an attestable claim to KMS requests; and 3) an audit-hash signer that appends an immutable HMACed signature to structured audit envelopes so downstream log archivists can verify integrity. Motivation: provide production-grade controls for cross-region operator actions and KMS usage without requiring customers to deploy bespoke middleware. This enables canary-safe rollout for dedicated/private deployments and gives SREs clear signals for policy violations.
Changes (high level):
- rbacv2: introduce TimeboundGrant and ApprovalQueue concepts plus a compact runtime evaluator and backpressure hooks for long-running approvals
- auth/kms: geofence prover service and request decorators that add geozone-assertion headers
- audit: introduce signed-audit-envelopes with an externalizable signature verifier and optional key-rotation support
- console/docs: UI bits for approval queue monitoring and admin docs for configuring geozone lists
- infra/helm: chart additions to enable the new services and RBAC operator bindings

Review thread (high level):
- Marco Nguyen: "Can the approval queue scale to noisy tenants? Suggest adding tenant-level rate limits and an exponential backoff for re-eval loops." Aisha: "Added tenant throttle and backoff in approval_queue.go; also added metrics (approval_queue.dequeue_rate) and a circuit-breaker."
- Priya Desai: "Audit signature key management needs to be procedurally audited; please include KMS-wrapped bootstrap keys and rotation tooling." Aisha: "Signer now supports KMS-wrapped primary keys and rotation via admin API; documented process in docs/security/timebound-rbac.md."
- Evan Chen: "Need explicit failure-mode behavior when geofence prover is unreachable (do we fail open or closed?)." Aisha: "Default is fail-closed for operator-impacting requests; added feature flag to allow fail-open for non-critical telemetry flows. Documented and covered in integration tests."

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged rollout: approval queue enabled for internal tenants and extended to beta customers after 2 weeks
- Gradual geofence enforcement: start as advisory (logs only) for non-production regions, then escalate to fail-closed for production regions after telemetry review
- Monitor: add alerts for high approval queue latency (>30s) and geofence prover error rate (>0.5%)
Notes for on-call and SRE:
- When the approval queue grows unexpectedly, check tenant throttle counters and reviewer backlog in console; restarting worker pods will not drop in-flight approvals due to durable queue.
- If audit-signer fails to initialize KMS key, service alerts as P1 and will not sign envelopes; fallback (unsigned envelopes) is allowed only behind an enterprise toggle.
Related: ENG-1124 (design), PM-233 (product spec).
